transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-29
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz; Marcus Chen; Priya Nair; Eli Thompson; Jon Park

Summary:
Quick vendor-assurance intake for Sylvan BioSciences. Focus on SIG/CAIQ path, SOC2 evidence, KMS options (BYOK vs Redwood-managed), data residency for EU subset of workloads, RBAC/SSO (SAML/Okta), and audit log retention. Agreed to exchange SIG spreadsheet and follow-up tech deep dive for private/VPC options.

Topics:
- SIG vs CAIQ preference / evidence mapping
- SOC 2 Type II availability and scope (subservice orgs?)
- KMS: BYOK, HSM, rotation policies
- Data residency & cross-border backups (EU PII concerns)
- RBAC, SSO, SCIM provisioning, least-privilege model
- Audit logs, retention, exportability, and SIEM integration

Transcript body:
[00:00] Lena Ortiz: Okay, hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro from Redwood — I'm Lena, account lead. Marcus is my SE, will cover the technical pieces.
[00:08] Priya Nair: Hi, Priya here. Thanks. We manage vendor risk at Sylvan so want to run through your SIG and encryption stuff.
[00:12] Marcus Chen: Hey all, Marcus. We'll try to be concise, and, uh, answer the SIG items you flagged in your intake form.
[00:18] Jon Park: Jon from procurement. We'll mostly watch but will also want to know timing for evidence.
[00:23] Eli Thompson: Eli, cloud arch. My main concerns are residency and network—VPC peering, private deployment if needed.
[00:29] Lena Ortiz: Perfect. So high-level, Redwood supports hosted, dedicated, and private modes. For SIG walkthrough we typically aim to map your critical items to our standard artifacts — SOC 2, ISO when applicable, architecture diagrams, and runbooks.
[00:41] Priya Nair: Do you have SOC 2 Type II? And does it cover the hosted API endpoints or only the control plane?
[00:48] Marcus Chen: We have SOC 2 Type II, yes. I'll drop the scope in the follow up. To call out, the report covers our hosted control plane and the inference runtime for the standard regions; for dedicated/private we provide additional attestations. Note: sometimes the wording in your SIG will expect subservice org disclosures—we can provide that mapping.
[01:05] Priya Nair: Okay good. Also pen testing — do you do external pentests and can you share summary?
[01:12] Lena Ortiz: Yes, annual external pentest; we can share a redacted summary and MOPs for patching cadence.
[01:18] Eli Thompson: For residency: we have EU-citizen PII that needs to remain in EU region. If using hosted, can you guarantee region-level control and no cross-region backup?
[01:26] Marcus Chen: We offer region pinning for model serving. Backups — ah — we do replicate certain metadata for durability; we can provide an architecture diagram and a data residency note that lists what's replicated and what's not. For strict requirements we often recommend Dedicated or Private.
[01:40] Priya Nair: And KMS, how does key management work? Customer-managed keys? HSM? Rotation?
[01:45] Marcus Chen: Short answer: yes, we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations. BYOK is supported for Dedicated/Private; hosted supports envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys or customer KMS for enterprise tiers. HSM-backed keys are available through our KMS partners — we can provide the KMS integration doc. Rotation policies: customer controls rotation in their KMS; Redwood will enforce key usage policies and we rotate internal wrapping keys.
[02:05] Priya Nair: Can you do bring-your-own-key with HSM such that Redwood never sees the plaintext keys?
[02:09] Marcus Chen: For Private deployments yes — the HSM is customer-controlled. For hosted, it's limited: we do envelope encryption where the CMK never leaves the KMS. I'll add a note clarifying the threat model because that's a common confusion — K V cache was, sorry, K V cache — um, KV cache, sometimes speech mis- — of course.
[02:28] Eli Thompson: About RBAC — we use Okta and SCIM for provisioning. Can we map roles to Redwood roles and get SSO for console and API?
[02:36] Lena Ortiz: Yes, SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning supported for the console, and we have token-based API scopes. RBAC can be configured to match your least-privilege model; we can produce a role matrix.
[02:46] Priya Nair: How about audit logs? We need to export to our SIEM and retain for 2 years. Is that supported?
[02:52] Marcus Chen: We support audit logs with configurable retention. For hosted there's a retention default but enterprise tiers can export logs to customer S3 or push to SIEM via syslog/collector. We'll get specifics in the evidence pack.
[03:05] Jon Park: What about third-party subprocessors? Do you have a list? We need to disclose that in our registry.
[03:10] Lena Ortiz: Yes, we maintain a subprocessors list—will attach the current one. It includes cloud infra partners and telemetry providers.
[03:16] Priya Nair: SIG vs CAIQ — which is easier for you to map? We usually ask for SIG but sometimes teams hand us CAIQ.
[03:22] Marcus Chen: We can map both; SIG preferred because it has the narrative. For CAIQ we can auto-populate answers for many items. Send whichever you have, and we'll annotate the source artifact for each answer.
[03:32] Eli Thompson: A couple of red flags in the intake: question 12 on data exports, question 27 on key custody, and question 44 on admin-level access. We need concrete evidence for those.
[03:41] Marcus Chen: Great — for admin-level access we have RBAC docs and an access review cadence; for key custody we'll provide the KMS flow diagram; for data exports we'll show the export controls and a sample export log.
[03:52] Priya Nair: What's the timeline to close a SIG? If we send the spreadsheet this week, how long?
[03:58] Lena Ortiz: Typically 5-10 business days depending on complexity and evidence availability. If a lot of custom evidence is needed (like private deployment architecture), it may take longer.
[04:09] Jon Park: Cost implications — if we ask for Dedicated or Private for residency, what's the buying cadence?
[04:15] Lena Ortiz: Dedicated is reserved capacity — monthly or annual commits. Private has an enterprise license plus onboarding. We'll share a one-pager after this.
[04:23] Eli Thompson: For the audit log export — does Redwood sanitize PII before sending to our SIEM?
[04:29] Marcus Chen: We can export logs with or without certain fields. We also support field redaction at export time; will include that in the log export doc.
[04:38] Priya Nair: Do you provide a SOC 2 bridge letter if there's a gap?
[04:43] Lena Ortiz: Yes, for procurement we can provide a bridge letter and a timeline for any remediation items.
[04:48] Eli Thompson: Any encryption-at-rest exceptions?
[04:51] Marcus Chen: No exceptions for customer data — all persisted customer data is encrypted at rest.
[04:55] Priya Nair: For evidence delivery — what format? A shared secure folder or portal?
[05:01] Lena Ortiz: We typically use a secure SFTP or transfer via a gated portal; for SIG spreadsheets we can accept uploads to a DocuShare link. We'll coordinate with your procurement team.
[05:10] Jon Park: Are there any security questionnaires you can't answer due to vendor IP?
[05:13] Marcus Chen: Occasionally we can't share low-level signature values or proprietary detection rules, but we provide summaries and redacted artifacts.
[05:20] Priya Nair: On the SOC 2 — do you segregate customer data logically or physically between tenants?
[05:26] Marcus Chen: Logical segregation; dedicated pools provide stronger isolation. For regulated workloads we recommend dedicated or private.
[05:32] Eli Thompson: For on-prem — latency concerns aside — do you support air-gapped installs?
[05:36] Marcus Chen: We have an on-prem package designed for air-gapped environments, with an offline installer and local key control. We'll discuss the logistics in the private deployment deep dive.
[05:46] Priya Nair: Can you describe the incident response process and SLA for breach notification?
[05:50] Lena Ortiz: We have documented incident response runbooks and a 72-hour initial notification SLA for incidents that impact customer data; severity-based escalation is in the IR policy. We'll share the IR summary.
[05:59] Eli Thompson: For SIEM integration — do you support ECS or a standard schema?
[06:03] Marcus Chen: We support common schemas and can map events to Elastic Common Schema (ECS) for easier ingestion.
[06:10] Priya Nair: A small picky item — in question mapping, sometimes the answers reference 'Redwood runtime' spelled 'Redwood runtime' but in our registry we need vendor legal name and product name separated.
[06:20] Lena Ortiz: Good catch — we'll make sure the mapping includes vendor legal name (Redwood Inference) and product name and versions.
[06:26] Jon Park: Any external audits other than SOC 2? ISO?
[06:29] Marcus Chen: We have SOC 2; ISO is in progress for some parts. We'll share the status note.
[06:35] Priya Nair: For employee access reviews, can you do quarterly attestations and provide proof?
[06:40] Marcus Chen: Yes, we have quarterly access reviews; we can show the attestation logs for the last two cycles (redacted).
[06:48] Eli Thompson: Okay, can we get a quick walkthrough of how a SIG item is mapped to an artifact in your pack?
[06:53] Marcus Chen: Sure — (screen share reference) for example, SIG question A1 maps to SOC 2 CC6, our access control policy, and our access review attestation. For key custody, we map to KMS integration doc plus the HSM certificate. We'll annotate each SIG row.
[07:12] Priya Nair: Great. We'll highlight question 12, 27, 44 as critical.
[07:16] Lena Ortiz: Noted. Action items again: we'll send SOC2 & pentest summary by Tuesday, Marcus will draft the KMS flow, and schedule a technical follow-up for next week.
[07:27] Jon Park: Timeline okay — procurement needs to know estimated closure date for contract signature.
[07:31] Lena Ortiz: If SIG is straightforward and no private deploy needed, 2-3 weeks. If private/dedicated architecture work required, 4-6 weeks plus procurement cycle.
[07:40] Priya Nair: Thanks. That helps.
[07:43] Eli Thompson: One last note — please include a short note on data deletion guarantees and deletion log availability.
[07:49] Marcus Chen: Will include deletion workflows and sample deletion logs.
[07:54] Lena Ortiz: Okay, we'll follow up with the docs. Thanks everyone.
[07:57] Priya Nair: Thanks, bye.

Call ended.

Notes on transcription: some words like "KV cache" transcribed as "K V cash" and vendor names occasionally garbled.

Evidence referenced during call:
- SOC 2 Type II report (to be attached)
- Redacted pen test summary
- KMS integration doc (BYOK/BYOK-HSM)
- Subprocessors list
- Audit log export doc and sample schema
- Mapping template for SIG/CAIQ answers

Recap (verbatim):
Lena Ortiz: We'll send SOC2 + pentest summary and subprocessor list by 2026-03-31. Marcus will create KMS/HSM flow note and log export doc by 2026-04-02. Priya will upload SIG spreadsheet with highlighted critical questions by 2026-04-05. Schedule technical deep dive for week of 2026-04-06 (Marcus + Eli).

End of transcript.
